rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī reports that Sūrat ʿAbasa is Meccan and counted as either forty or forty-one verses.
rows.anchor: أربعون أو إحدى وأربعون آية مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbasa describes a frowning or sour expression, while tawallā means that he turned away.
rows.anchor: العبس والعبوس ترش روى شدن يعني ترش كرد روى خودرا

rows.speaker: المبصريون
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Muhammad, and Basran grammarians take the blind man's arrival as the cause of his turning away because the phrase is nearby.
rows.anchor: الضمير لمحمد عليه السلام وهو علة لتولي على رأي المبصريين لقربه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness can mean loss of sight or, figuratively, loss of insight; the definite article identifies the familiar Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: والعمى افتقاد البصر ويقال : في افتقاد البصيرة أيضا ولام الأعمى للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man was Ibn Umm Maktum, an early emigrant and the Prophet's second muezzin; the Prophet deputized him in Medina twice, or according to another report three times.
rows.anchor: وهو ابن أم مكتوم المؤذن الثاني لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأذان

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that Bilal calls the night adhān, so people may eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls.
rows.anchor: إن بلالا يؤذن بليل فكلوا واشربوا حتى يؤذن ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner; Qadisiyya was where ʿUmar's forces defeated the Persians and seized abundant spoils.
rows.anchor: قال أنس رضي الله عنه رأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع وله راية سوداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authorities disagree whether Ibn Umm Maktum was ʿAbd Allah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik or ʿAmr ibn Qays ibn Zāʾida; the latter is identified as Khadīja's cousin.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في اسم ابن أم مكتوم فقيل هو عبد الله بن شريج بن مالك

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Saʿdī calls the Kashshāf's identification of Umm Maktum as the name of Ibn Umm Maktum's father's mother mistaken; Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and others say she was his mother, ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir.
rows.anchor: وقال السعدي هو وهم فقد نص ابن عبد البر وغيره إنها أمه واسمها عاتكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Mecca, Ibn Umm Maktum approached while the Prophet was inviting Quraysh leaders to Islam, hoping their conversion would draw others, since people follow their leaders; he repeatedly asked to be taught.
rows.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك في مكة وعنده صناديد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum could not see that the Prophet was occupied; the Prophet may not have heard him because of low voices, or may have disliked interrupting his conversation and turning from the leaders.
rows.anchor: إذا السمع لا يكفي في العلم بالتشاغل بل لا بد من الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum left grief-stricken and feared the Prophet's frown and turning away meant God disapproved of him, whereupon the verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: فرجع ابن أم مكتوم محزونا خائفا أن يكون عبوسه وأعراضه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification is inwardly cleansing from sins, while remembrance is adornment through obedience; the educator should seek the learner's purification, and the learner should study to cleanse the heart of misguidance and ignorance, not for worldly status or appearance.
rows.anchor: من باب التخلية عن الآثام وقوله أو يذكر من باب التحلية ببعض الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative particle wa-aw joins remembrance to purification under the hope expressed earlier, and fatanafaʿahu is accusative as the response to laʿalla, by analogy with layta.
rows.anchor: فقوله أو يذكر عطف على بزكي داخل معه في حكم الترجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative fatanafaʿahu is construed as the response to laʿalla, in the manner of a response to layta.
rows.anchor: فتنفعه الذكرى بالنصب على جواب لعل تشبيها له بليت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who set out to purify unbelievers who reject guidance should not expect them to be purified or reminded.
rows.anchor: من تصدى لتزكيتهم من الكفرة لا يرجى منهم التزكي والتذكر أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ammā marks a contrast; the person who considers himself independent rejects faith and the knowledge and insights contained in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: {أما} للتفضيل {من استغنى} عن الإيمان وعما عندك من العلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tataṣaddā is shortened by deleting one of its two tāʾs; its full form is tataṣaddā, meaning to turn toward him and devote attention to guiding him.
rows.anchor: بحذف إحدى التاءين تخفيفا أي تتصدى وتتعرض بالإقبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's attentiveness to the self-satisfied man rather than the blind seeker is especially discouraged: a noble person does not eagerly approach someone who turns away.
rows.anchor: وفيه مزيد تنفير له عليه السلام ، عن مصاحبتهم فإن الإقبال على المدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddī means exposing oneself to something, attending to it, and being preoccupied with it; its opposite is to turn away from it.
rows.anchor: والتصدي للشيء التعرض والتقيد به والاهتمام بشأنه وضده التشاغل عنه

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt explains taṣaddī as eager exposure to something, like a thirsty person seeking water.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" التصدي التعرض للشيء على حرص كتعرض الصديان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive taṣaddī from ṣadad, what faces or confronts one, with one of the doubled letters replaced by a weak letter.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أصل تصدي تصدد من الصدد وهو ما استقبلك وجاء قبالتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet bears no blame or burden if the self-satisfied man does not become purified by Islam; there is no need to prioritize him over someone who has accepted guidance.
rows.anchor: وليس عليك بأس ووزر ووبال في أن لا يتزكى ذلك المستغني بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not press Islam upon a person with no receptivity who loves the present world and is blind to the hereafter; the verse also belittles the one who turns away.
rows.anchor: وكيف تحرض على الإسلام من ليس له قابلية وقد خلق على حب الدنيا والعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is negative; the implied preposition fī is linked to an omitted noun, and the clause is circumstantial to taṣaddā, reinforcing the rebuke.
rows.anchor: فما نافية وكلمة في المقدرة متعلقة باسم ما وهو محذوف والجملة حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā commands the Prophet to stop giving attention to the self-satisfied man while leaving the seeker without guidance.
rows.anchor: {كلا} انزجر من التصدي للمستغني والإعراض عن إرشاد المسترشد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Gabriel recited these verses to the Prophet, whose face changed as though dust had been scattered over it; he awaited God's judgment until kallā relieved him.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : لما تلا جبرائيل هذه الآيات على النبي عليه السلام عاد وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to repeat this conduct because it is unworthy of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي لا تفعل مثل ذلك فإنه غير لائق بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in innahā refers to the Qur'an, with grammatical gender following the predicate tadhkira.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن والتأنيث باعتبار الخبر وهو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder that people must heed and act upon.
rows.anchor: أي موعظة يجب أن يتعظ بها ويعمل بموجبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever wishes remembers the Qur'an by retaining it without forgetting, or by taking heed of it; there is no need to devote special attention to someone who rejects it.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن أي حفظه ولم ينسه أو اتعظ به ومن رغب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in pages can modify reminder through an implied description, with the intervening words parenthetical to encourage its preservation, or serve as a second predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: {في صحف} جمع صحفة وكل مكتوب عند العرب صحيفة وهو متعلق بمضمر

rows.speaker: السجاوندي
rows.claim: Al-Sajāwandī treats in pages as the predicate of an omitted subject and marks a required pause after whoever wishes to remember, avoiding the false implication that a person's choice is recorded in God's Qur'an pages.
rows.anchor: والسجاوندي على إنه خبر محذوف أي وهي في صحف حتى وضع علامة الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are either in the seventh heaven or elevated in rank and renown; famously, they are kept at Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: {مرفوعة} أي في السماء السابعة أو مرفوعة المقدار والذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are protected from contact with devils.
rows.anchor: {مطهرة} منزهة عن مساس أيدي الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The safara are angelic scribes who copy scriptures from the Preserved Tablet; the word is connected with writing that discloses and clarifies.
rows.anchor: كتبة من الملائكة ينتسخون الكتب من اللوح على إنه جمع سافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is likened to travel because it uncovers a person's character; a writer is called a sāfir because writing makes things clear, and the word is especially associated with angels though linguistically broader.
rows.anchor: وسمى السفر بفتحتين سفرا لأنه يسفر ويكسف عن أخلاق المرء

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl says the pages are called purified because only purified angels touch them.
rows.anchor: فقال القفال في وجه لما لم يسمها إلا الملائكة المطهرون أضيف التطهير

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī identifies the purified beings in 56:79 as these noble angelic scribes.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي إن المراد في قوله تعالى : [الواقعة : 79-16]{لا يمسه إلا المطهرون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in the hands of scribes most naturally modifies pages, meaning pages held or written by scribes; some pause after purified to prevent a mistaken attachment to that word.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن تكون في محل الجر على إنها صفة لصحف أي في صحف كائنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are noble in God's sight through nearness and honor, or gracious toward believers by seeking forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: كرام} عند الله بالقرب والشرف فهو من الكرامة جمع كريم أو متعطفين

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says their nobility means they do not accompany Adam's descendants during intercourse or while relieving themselves, referring to the angels called noble writers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله يريد أنهم يتكرمون أن يكونوا مع ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barara may mean pious, because the angels transcend materiality and attachments; obedient to God; or truthful in their oaths, from barr in an oath.
rows.anchor: {بررة} اتقياء لتقدسها عن المواد ونزاهة جواهرها عن التعلقات أو مطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a curse against the human being, the most dreadful worldly calamity; construing killing as cursing denotes spiritual destruction, an even harsher punishment, and here the target is the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: {قتل الانسان} دعاء عليه بأشنع الدعوات فإن القتل غاية شدائد الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā akfarahu means how intense his disbelief and ingratitude are despite God's abundant beneficence.
rows.anchor: ما أشد كفره بالله مع كثرة إحسانه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation portrays excessive ingratitude; it is not literal divine surprise, since true surprise comes from ignorance of a cause, but a divine expression inviting people to marvel at his unbelief and recognize his deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: تعجب من إفراطه في الكفران أي على صورته فإن حقيقة التعجب إنما تتصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the unbeliever merits God's curse and magnified condemnation because he failed to know his Maker and himself, through whose knowledge he would know his Maker.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لعن الله الكافر وعظم كفره حيث لم يعرف صانعه ولم يعرف

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the Arabic curse and exclamation are rhetorical, not evidence of divine inability to avenge or ignorance; they express intense wrath and emphatic blame for a heinous deed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : هذا الدعاء وارد على أسلوب كلام العرب فهو ليس من قبيل دعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā akfarahu is a reproachful question asking what drove the person to disbelief.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما أكفره استفهاما بمعنى التقريع والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being may mean the self-satisfied person previously described, or humanity as a class including him and others.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الإنسان إما من استغنى عن القرآن المذكور نعوته وإما الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question reminds the human being of his humble origin, exposing how unfitting pride, arrogance, and ingratitude are toward his benefactor.
rows.anchor: من أي شيء حقير مهين خلقه يعني نمى انديشدكه خداي تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nutfa is a filthy, lowly drop; someone created from it has no basis for arrogance toward the benefactor who gave him a beautiful form.
rows.anchor: {من نطفة} قذرة {خلقه} فمن كان أصله مثل هذا الشيء الحقير كيف يليق به

rows.speaker: السجاوندي
rows.claim: Al-Sajāwandī pauses after from a drop, supplying another created him from what precedes and treating created him, then proportioned him as a new explanatory sentence.
rows.anchor: وقف السجاوندي على قوله من نطفة حتى وضع عليه علامة الوقف المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent construction connects from a drop to created him and does not pause there; taking created him proportioned him as a new sentence avoids redundancy because creation itself entails measured quantities and qualities.
rows.anchor: ومن جعله متعلقا بما بعده على ما هو الظاهر لم يقف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepared the human being with suitable organs, shapes, quantities, qualities, and capacities, each fitted to its benefit and proper use.
rows.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له ويليق به من الأعضاء والأشكال أي أحدثه بمقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, proportioning describes development through successive stages, from a clot and a morsel of flesh to completion, as male or female and wretched or blessed.
rows.anchor: أو فقدره أطوار إلى أن تم خلقه فالتقدير المتفرع على الخلق مأخوذ

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya interprets what the soul sent forward as good or evil deeds brought from potential into actuality, and what it left behind as intentions retained in potential.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : علمت نفس ما قدمت أخرجت من القوة إلى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge of what each soul did answers when the preceding cosmic events occur; the repeated when clauses intensify their terrors, all within the single period from the first trumpet blast to judgment.
rows.anchor: قوله علمت الخ جواب إذاأمي إذا وقعت هذه الأشياء وخربت الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Detailed knowledge comes when people read their records and are reckoned; they gain general awareness at resurrection as the obedient see signs of happiness and sinners signs of misery.
rows.anchor: فالمراد العلم التفصيلي الذي يحصل عند قراءة الكتب والمحاسبة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh takes knowing all deeds as a metonym for being recompensed for them, with the passage warning against sin and urging obedience.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في حواشيه العلم بجميع ذلك كناية عن المجازاة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address covers all disobedient people, not only unbelievers, since it falls between the general statement about every soul and its elaboration concerning the righteous.
rows.anchor: يا اأيها الانسان} يعم جميع العصاة ولا خصوص له بالكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later plural accusation that they deny the judgment can use a singular generic human, just as one person in a clan's action may be attributed to the clan.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله بل تكذبون بالدين فمن قبيل بنوا فلان

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the intended person is Umayya ibn Khalaf, while the general wording also applies to others; other reports name al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or al-Aswad ibn Kalada.
rows.anchor: قال الامام السهيلي رحمه الله قوله : يا أيها الإنسان يريد أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in Zahrat al-Riyāḍ says a man struck the Prophet on the crown, was thrown down by him, then asked for safety and promised not to harm him; the Prophet released him.
rows.anchor: وفي زهرة الرياض ضرب على يافوخ رسول الله عليه السلام ، فأخذه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproachful question asks what deceived and emboldened a person to disobey God and feel safe from punishment despite the calamities and deeds awaiting him.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام بمعنى الاستهجان والتوبيخ والمعنى أي شيء خدعك وجرأك على عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To deceive someone regarding another is to embolden him and make him feel safe from danger on that person's account, though the danger is real.
rows.anchor: يقال غره بفلان إذا جرأه عليه وأمنه المحذور من جهته مع إنه غير مأمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God generous does not justify complacency, despite Satan's suggestion that one may sin because God is generous; divine generosity should instead increase faith, obedience, and avoidance of sin.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان كرمه تعالى للإيذان بأنه ليس مما يصلح أن يكون مدار الاغترار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited this verse, he said that ignorance had deceived the person.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قرأها غره جهله

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Baṣrī says that, by God, Satan deceived him.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري رحمه الله غره والله شيطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's generosity calls for fear of disobedience: neglecting an oppressor would wrong the oppressed, and generosity cannot mean treating the hostile and devoted alike; paired divine names include mercy and painful punishment.
rows.anchor: من حيث إن إهمال الظالم ينافي كونه كريما بالنسبة إلى المظلوم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a sound hadith, God draws the believer near, covers him, asks him to acknowledge his sins until he fears ruin, then says He concealed them in this life and forgives him today.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح) : إن الله يدني المؤمن فيضع عليه كنفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of God as creator further establishes His lordship and explains His generosity: giving existence is better than nonexistence, and the ability to originate implies the ability to recreate.
rows.anchor: {الذى خلقك} صفة ثانية مقررة للربوبية مبينة للكرم لأن الخلق إعطاء لوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the limbs sound and balanced so each performs its intended benefit, such as grasping by the hand, walking by the foot, and seeing by the eye.
rows.anchor: أي جعل أعضاءك سوية سليمة معدة لمنفعها أي بحيث يترتب على كل عضو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God balanced corresponding limbs and features, such as the two hands, legs, ears, eyes, and sides of the body, without disproportion.
rows.anchor: عدل بعض تلك الأعضاء ببعض بحيث أعتدلت ولم تتفاوت مثل أن تكون إحدى اليدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anatomists say the two sides of the body match in bones, shape, veins, arteries, and nerves.
rows.anchor: قال علماء التشريح إنه تعالى ركب جانبي هذه الجنة على التساوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ʿadalaka means He turned you away from an ugly animal form and gave you a beautiful form distinct from other creatures, as in 95:4.
rows.anchor: ويقال عدله عن الطرق أي صرفه فيكون المعنى فصرفك عن الخلقة المكروهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant with doubled dāl, faʿaddalaka, means that God made the human being proportionate and harmonious without disparity, close in sense to the lighter form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فعدلك بالتشديد أي صيرك معتدلا متناسب الخلق من غير تفاوت

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd says God perfected the human form through knowledge and adjusted it through faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره تسوية الخلقة بلمعرفة وتعديلها بالإيمان

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn says God brought the human being into existence and subjected all created things to him, without subjecting him to any of them.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون قدس سره أوجدك فسخر لك المكونات أجمع ولم يسخرك لشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to compete outwardly encourages and exhorts; inwardly it obligates faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: والأمر للتحضيض والترغيب ظاهرا وللوجوب باطنا بوجوب الإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competition is striving to obtain a precious, desirable thing, each person wishing to possess it exclusively; the root is also associated with the soul's value.
rows.anchor: وأصل التنافس التغالب في الشيء النفيس أي المرغوب كأن كل واحد من الشخصين

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī derives competition from a precious thing coveted by everyone, each person wanting it for himself and begrudging it to others.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : أصله من الشيء النفيس الذي يحرص عليه نفوس الناس

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines competition as disciplining oneself to resemble and catch up with the virtuous without harming anyone else.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" المنافسة مجاهدة النفس للتشبه بالأفاضل واللحوق بهم من غير إدخال ضرر

rows.speaker: ذو النون المصري
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn lists signs of true spiritual competition: a heart attached to the goal, eagerness when it is mentioned, solitude, regretful tears, delight in remembrance and Qur'an, gratitude, and seeking intimate prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ذو النون المصري رحمه الله ، علامة التنافس تعلق القلب به وطيران الضمير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase its mixture is from Tasnīm coordinates with its seal and supplies another description of the same pure drink.
rows.anchor: {ومزاجه من تسنيم} عطف على ختامه صفة أخرى لرحيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnīm is the name of a spring in the Garden of Eden, named for elevation, either its superior rank among drinks or its descent from above.
rows.anchor: وهو علم العين بعينها تجري من جنة عدن سميت بالتسنيم الذي هو مصدر سنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Tasnīm flows through the air into their vessels and stops when they are full so not a drop falls to the ground and no drawing of water is needed.
rows.anchor: روى إنها تجري في الهواء متسنمة فتنصب في أوانيهم فإذا امتلأت أمسك الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAynan is accusative as an expression of praise or specification, with an implied I mean.
rows.anchor: {عينا} نصب على المدح والاختصاص أي بتقدير أعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those brought near to God drink Tasnīm pure, while it is mixed for the other people of Paradise, the companions of the right; the preposition may be extra or mean from.
rows.anchor: {يشرب بها المقربون} من جناب الله قربا معنويا روحانيا أي يشربون ماءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the spiritual Paradise, Tasnīm signifies knowledge and love of God and the joy of seeing His face; pure drink symbolizes unalloyed divine love, while mixed drink reflects mixed love.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن التسنيم في الجنة الروحانية هو معرفة الله ومحبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky of the animal spirit parts from the human spirit and disappears; the body's earth is spread when the spirit leaves, emptied of its spirit, powers, life, temperament, composition, and form.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى انشقاق سماء الروح الحيوانية بانفراجها عن الروح الإنساني

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya reads the spirit's sky as separating from the dark cloud of the commanding self and yielding to divine effusion, while human souls' earth is extended for its Lord and sheds human conditions.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى انشقاق سماء الروح عن ظلمة غيم النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address applies to every accountable person—believer, unbeliever, or sinner—individually, more emphatically than an undifferentiated plural address.
rows.anchor: جنس الإنسان الشامل للمؤمن والكافر والعاصي فالخطاب عام لكل مكلف على سبيل البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhḥ is strenuous effort that affects the self; the related words denote hardship, toil, and severe striving, from the image of scratching the skin.
rows.anchor: الكدح جهد النفس في العمل والكد فيه بحيث يؤثر فيها والجهد بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person labors with difficulty toward meeting the Lord, meaning the time of meeting at death and the subsequent states represented as meeting.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إنك جاهد ومجد أي ساع باجتهاد ومشقة إلى لقاء ربك أي إلى وقت لقائه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked how to labor after the pens had dried and destinies been decreed, the Prophet said to act, for each person is made easy for what he was created to do.
rows.anchor: فقال اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person will inevitably meet the reward of his good or evil work, with no evasion or escape; worldly effort is in reality a path to its afterlife recompense.
rows.anchor: فملاق له أي لجزاء عملك من خير وشر عقيب ذلك لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should undertake worldly actions that save one in the hereafter and avoid those that bring ruin, shame, and disgrace.
rows.anchor: فعليك أن تباشر في الدنيا بما ينجيك في العقبى واحذر عما يهلكك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the remorseful await mercy, the self-admiring await condemnation, and every worker will advance to what he sent ahead.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث النادم ينتظرالرحمة والمعجب ينتظر المقت وكل عامل سيقدم

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī says receiving the record behind one's back means returning to the darkness of the animal spirit and body, being restored to animal forms, crying for destruction in spiritual perdition, and entering the fire of nature's effects.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : وأما من أوتى كتابه وراء ظهره أي جهته التي تلي الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innahu introduces the reason for the preceding statement; the clause is a fresh explanation of its cause.
rows.anchor: إنه} أي لأن فالجملة استئناف لبيان علة ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī ahlihi can mean among his family and relatives or with them, with all of them happy together.
rows.anchor: {فى أهله} فيما بين أهله وعشيرته أو معهم على أنهم جميعا كانوا مسرورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase came to me with a group demonstrates that fī can mean together with.
rows.anchor: كما يقال جاءني فلان في جماعة أي معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned person lived in luxury, arrogance, and delight, occupied with wealth, status, and pleasures.
rows.anchor: {مسرورا} مترفا بطرا مستبشرا يعني شادان ونازان بمال فإني وجاه نا يدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever was carefree about the hereafter and is repaid with lasting grief, while the believer carries lament in the heart and is repaid with lasting joy; spiritually, the upper spirit receives its record in the right hand and the lower self from behind.
rows.anchor: والحاصل إنه كان الكافر في الدنيا فارغا عن هم الآخرة وكان له مزمار في قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, his family represents the luminous spiritual faculties or the dark bodily faculties, corresponding to the upper spirit or lower self.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة أيضا إلى الروح العلوي الذ يؤتى كتابه بيمينه وإلى النفس السفلية

rows.speaker: الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanārī, in his Tafsīr al-Fātiḥa, says ẓann here means certainty.
rows.anchor: ظن} تيقن كما في "تفسير الفاتحة" للفناري

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān takes ẓann in its ordinary sense of supposition, not certainty.
rows.anchor: وقال في "فتح الرحمن" الظن هنا على بابه بمعنى الحسبان لا الظن الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever's joy is explained by his supposition that he would never return to God, since he denied resurrection; ḥawr means to return or come back.
rows.anchor: لن يرجع إلى الله تكذيبا للمعاد والحور الرجوع والمحار المرجع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he learned the meaning of yaḥūr by hearing a Bedouin woman tell her daughter to return and hearing the expression return to your family.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما كنت أدري ما معنى يحور حتى سمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression seeking refuge from ḥawr after kawr means returning from a good state; a ḥawwārī is a fuller because he restores cloth to whiteness.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث نعوذ بالله من الحور بعد الكور أي الرجوع عن حالة جميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balā affirms the negated proposition: indeed he will certainly return, contrary to his belief.
rows.anchor: {بلى} إيجاب لما بدع لن أي بلى ليحورن البتة وليس الأمر كما يظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees the person and every deed that warrants recompense; divine wisdom therefore requires resurrection, accounting, and repayment rather than leaving deeds without consequence, warning all accountable people against sin.
rows.anchor: بحيث لا تخفى منها خافية فلا بد من رجعه وحسابه وجزائه عليها حتما

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ṭibāq as placing one thing over another according to its measure, as matching one shoe to another; the word does not cover both superposition and mere correspondence.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : المطابقة من لأسماء المتضايفة وهو أن يجعل الشيء فوق آخر بقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes ṭabaq as the plural of ṭabaqa, a level or rank, which better fits the image of mounting one level after another.
rows.anchor: وقيل الطبق جمع طبقة وهي المرتبة وهو الأوفق للركوب المنبىء عن الاعتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings will pass through successive states, each a level in severity, from death through the terrors of resurrection until settling in one of the two abodes.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لتركبن أحوالا بعد أحوال هي طبقات في الشدة بعضها أرفع من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular reading addresses the human being by grammatical form, while the plural reading addresses humanity collectively.
rows.anchor: وقرىء لتركبن بالإفراد على خطاب الإنسان باعتبار اللفظ لا باعتبار شموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAn ṭabaq may be accusative as an adjective of ṭabaqan, meaning a level surpassed, or circumstantial with the pronoun in l-tarkabunna; ʿan retains its usual sense of passing beyond.
rows.anchor: ومحل عن طبق النصب على إنه صفة لطبقا أي طبقا مجاوز الطبق أو حال

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh explains ʿan as after: once a person passes one thing and reaches another, the second comes after the first; ʿan also implies distance and transition.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ عن هنا بمعنى بعد لأن الإنسان إذا صار إلى شيء مجاوزا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya addresses the human heart turning to God through spiritual disciplines and struggles, passing through corresponding severe states such as hunger, night vigil, silence, and solitude.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يخاطب القلب الإنساني المتوجه إلى الله بأنواع الرياضات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given their future condition, what prevents people from believing when the reasons for faith support one another?
rows.anchor: {فما لهم لا يؤمنون} أي إذا كان حالهم يوم القيامة ما ذكر فأي شيء لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the self, its desires, and natural human faculties prevent the heart from believing and obeying the law, the manners of the spiritual path, and the traces of ultimate reality.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى النفس والهوى والقوى البشرية الطبيعية وعدم إيمانهم بالقلب

words: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause is circumstantial and coordinated with the preceding clause, describing their state when the Qur'an is recited to them.
rows.anchor: جملة شرطية محلها النصب على الحالية نسقا على ما قبلها

words: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to bow or submit when the Prophet, one of his Companions, or another Muslim recites the Qur'an is blameworthy: as speakers of Arabic, they should recognize its inimitability and divine origin, affirm Muhammad's prophethood, and obey him.
rows.anchor: أي أي مانع لهم حال عدم سجودهم وخضوعهم واستكانتهم عند قراءة النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means not performing prostration when the specific prostration verse is recited, rather than failing to prostrate at any Qur'an recitation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد به نفس السجود عند تلاوة آية السجدة على أن يكون المراد
